background.text: The terms of Francis I, the title of first painter, engineer, and architect of the King and a large pension, purchased not finished works but the presence of Leonardo himself at the court. The paralysis of the right hand reported by Beatis marks the physical close of his painting; the same account dwells on the mass of manuscripts and anatomical drawings, confirming that the labor of the last years had already shifted to the ordering of the papers. The documented work of the period comprises the plan for a new palace and canal system at Romorantin (1517 to 1518, manuscript studies and survey on the ground A ) and the production of court festivals: the celebrations of May 1518 for the baptism of the Dauphin and the wedding of Lorenzo de' Medici, and the restaging of the Festa del Paradiso at Cloux on 19 June 1518, reported in ambassadorial dispatches A . As the will directed, the body was buried in the collegiate church of Saint Florentin within the château. The church, ruined in the revolutionary years, was demolished early in the nineteenth century (about 1806 to 1808); in 1863 an excavation conducted by Arsène Houssaye recovered remains presumed to be Leonardo's, and in 1874 they were placed in the chapel of Saint Hubert on the ramparts. The present tomb is thus a translation, and the identification of the remains has never risen above presumption D .
